volctx.headline: VIX 19.92 (stress, 93rd percentile, rising) governs SPX/SPY/XSP
volctx.hedge: VIX is in STRESS: hedge flows are at their largest per move; gamma and vanna flows both scale, so levels break more easily and rebounds come from vol falling back (vanna bid), not from walls. Vol is rising: a +1 pt IV move makes dealers SELL 602 contracts, adding to downside pressure.
volctx.vanna: Vol is rising: a +1 pt IV move makes dealers SELL 602 contracts, adding to downside pressure.
volctx.vomma: Vomma negative: dealer vega shrinks as IV rises, so a vol spike self-limits dealer vega hedging.
volctx.divergence: VXN and VIX agree (percentiles within 25 pts, same direction): no relative-stress signal between Nasdaq and S&P books.

session.window: 09:30 ET to 10:10 ET (tracking stops one hour before the close; the final hour is read as the handoff)
session.charm_headline: Charm is positive to the close: +786 ES contracts, moderate. Time alone makes dealers BUY into the close. Since the open it has gone from +904 to +786 (fading).
session.interaction: VIX is rising: one more vol point makes dealers SELL 602 contracts. That OFFSETS charm (opposite direction); combined drift into the close ~+184 contracts (upward) if vol keeps moving 1 pt.
session.closing: Net gamma is negative (-22M/1%): dealers amplify the charm drift, so the move into the close can extend. 350 min to the close.

observed.reading: Net dealer hedge change is negligible (+79.8 contracts vs 3603 for a 1% move): hedging did not drive this window.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: A rising dollar is the classic headwind for gold: it adds pressure to a break lower.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move in gold.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar cushions gold and slows a break.
states.up: A falling dollar supports an upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Falling yields lower the opportunity cost of holding gold: it cushions a break.
states.up: Falling yields support the upside move (lower real-rate opportunity cost).

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Rising yields raise the opportunity cost of gold and add pressure to a break.
states.up: Rising yields cap the upside move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising equity volatility can bring safe-haven bids that offset a break, or forced liquidation that adds to it: direction is not fixed by the options data.
states.up: Rising volatility can add safe-haven demand and support an upside move.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility reduces safe-haven demand and adds mild pressure.
states.up: Falling volatility reduces safe-haven demand and limits the upside.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.

factors.label: US dollar (DXY)
factors.note: no DXY feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Dollar strength tightens financial conditions and weighs on foreign-earnings translation, so it adds selling pressure to the break.
states.up: A rising dollar works against an upside move: rallies run into tighter conditions and lose follow-through.

states.label: falling
states.dn: A falling dollar eases conditions and can slow the break: it is a cushion, not a floor.
states.up: A falling dollar eases conditions and supports the upside move.

factors.label: Bonds (price)
factors.note: no BONDS feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising (yields falling)
states.dn: Rising bonds during an equity break reads as flight to safety: it confirms risk-off and does not cushion equities.
states.up: Rising bonds with rising equities is a supportive, falling-yield backdrop for duration-sensitive indices.

states.label: falling (yields rising)
states.dn: Falling bonds (rising yields) while equities break adds a valuation squeeze on top of the options-driven selling.
states.up: Falling bonds (rising yields) caps upside for long-duration growth names and limits the move.

factors.label: Volatility index
factors.note: no VOL feed connected: the state below is a hypothesis you choose, not a reading

states.label: rising
states.dn: Rising volatility raises dealer vega/vanna demands: lower puts and hedges get re-priced and dealer hedging accelerates the break.
states.up: Rising volatility during a rally is unusual: it signals hedging demand and makes upside breaks less reliable.

states.label: falling
states.dn: Falling volatility during a break suggests an orderly pullback: vanna/charm flows turn supportive and the break tends to stall.
states.up: Falling volatility supports the rally: vanna flows turn dealers into buyers.

pairs.x: Rising dollar AND rising bonds while the index breaks: classic risk-off. The dollar and the bond bid both drain risk appetite, and neither cushions equities.
Rising dollar with falling bonds: a rates-driven tightening. It pressures long-duration index weights hardest and is the most damaging combination for valuation.
Falling dollar with rising bonds: easing conditions. A break in this setting is more likely to be technical/positioning and to find buyers sooner.
Falling dollar with falling bonds: mixed signal (inflation/reflation). Index breaks are less macro-driven; options flows dominate.
